**#599: root cause found, high confidence.**
- Chromium 145's browser process calls `setenv("FC_FONTATIONS","1")` from a thread-pool thread about 50 ms after launch. When the variable is absent, glibc reallocates `environ` and frees the old array. Meanwhile another thread, such as the D-Bus thread, the main thread or the resolver, can be in `getenv()` scanning that array.
- All 3 crashes fault at the same instruction, `libc+0x48806`, which is the compare inside glibc's `getenv` scanning loop. The garbage entry matches a freed PartitionAlloc slot. The first letter of the name being looked up (`r13`) is D, T or R, and I confirmed the D one in the binary as the call to `dbus_bus_get_private`.
- The issue listed one crash; I found 3 in about 3,600 e2e jobs: 10-11 20:28 (perf), 10-13 12:40 (reader) and 10-14 10:41 (the one on the issue).
- I downloaded the exact Chrome 145.0.7632.6 headless shell. `environ` moved in 23 of 23 plain launches. With a `getenv` made to stall in the browser, 31 of 40 launches crashed with the same signature; with `FC_FONTATIONS=1` preset, 0 of 40 crashed and the array never moved.
- Fix: PR #660 launches the browser with `FC_FONTATIONS=1` already set, which is the value Chromium writes itself (one constant in `playwright.config.js`).
- The proper owner is Chromium. I could not file upstream, and the proxy refused a search of `microsoft/playwright` (HTTP 403), which I did not work around. The upstream report text is in the #599 comment.

- `hex()` pipes the value to `grep -Eqx`, which matches per line, so a value passes if any one line is a valid fingerprint.
